principle: A concern has durable meaning upstream of GitHub. Issues coordinate it, branches execute it, pull requests propose a durable result, and receipts or observations show what happened. Execution artifacts never become the source of product meaning.

source_projection.rule: Project source from canonical references the ticket already carries. Do not mint a parallel source identity in GitHub when an existing repository identifier already names the meaning.

product_intent.resolution: Each canonical capability resolves upward through contracts/product-canon.json to its journeys, promises, and Ground claims.

evidence.resolution: These point at the observation, receipt, or exact target that caused or tested the concern.

governance.resolution: These identify a binding rule or authority seam when policy rather than product capability is the immediate source.

coordination.resolution: These connect the concern to other concern records without redefining their semantics.

source_projection.fallback: When no canonical ticket field can name the source, the issue body may carry a Source section with an exact repository address or owner-directed interaction reference. This is an address, not a new semantic definition.

derived_from.meaning: This concern exists because the named source is not yet realized, proven, reconciled, or otherwise settled.

depends_on.meaning: This concern cannot reach its next transition until the named concern or artifact exists.

advances.meaning: The result reduces the unsatisfied concern but does not settle it. The issue remains open with the next unsatisfied state visible.

satisfies.meaning: The durable result settles the concern represented by the issue. The issue may close once the result and required evidence exist.

supersedes.meaning: A named successor concern or durable result now owns the remaining meaning. The old issue closes only when that successor is explicit.

execution_link.branch_link_rule: Link a branch to its concern through the pull request that carries the branch and names the issue. Do not maintain a second branch registry or write the branch name back into the issue merely to duplicate GitHub's graph.
execution_link.pull_request_rule: Every pull request names the concern it advances, satisfies, or supersedes. Use GitHub's Closes syntax only when the relation is satisfies; a merely advancing pull request must not close the concern.
execution_link.merge_rule: Merge proves only that a result entered the base. Merge alone does not prove satisfaction.

requires: the durable result exists on the intended base
the pull request records advances, satisfies, or supersedes for the concern it carries
the concern's remaining standing is explicit after the merge
open dependent pull requests and shared branch uses are accounted for
a merged remote head is retired when contracts/external-effect-authorization.json admits retirement
local contained branch, worktree, and live claim or session state are retired when the participant controls them
a satisfied concern is closed; a superseded concern names its successor before closing; an advanced concern remains open

adoption.historical_rule: Do not mint cleanup tickets merely to retrofit metadata. Enrich an old concern when it is touched for real work or when source/settlement information directly enables absorption or closure.
adoption.new_work_rule: A newly minted meaningful concern must be traceable to product intent, evidence, governance, or a named parent concern before it justifies new execution inventory.

defeating_cases: a branch or pull request becomes the semantic source of the concern
the same source meaning is copied into a second GitHub-owned registry
a merged pull request closes an issue that it only advances
a branch is retained after satisfaction without a concrete dependency or authority reason
historical issues are converted into new cleanup work solely to satisfy this policy
source attribution is treated as authority or evidence of satisfaction
